title: Trace propagation across services
summary: One user request crosses agents, MCP servers, A2A peers and queues. Propagating W3C trace context over each hop, in HTTP headers or MCP params._meta, keeps it one trace. Some hops need correlation ids instead.
useIf: A single request touches several processes and you want one trace, not five unrelated ones.
avoidIf: You forward baggage or trace context to parties that should not see it, or assume every framework propagates it for you.

explain.md: W3C Trace Context defines the `traceparent` header: `00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>`, plus `tracestate`. Level 1 is a W3C Recommendation (2021-11-23). Level 2 is still a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2024-03-28) [[r8]]. Over HTTP, OpenTelemetry instrumentation injects and extracts these headers for you.

**MCP** has no HTTP-only assumption, so the conventions inject `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage` into the request's `params._meta` using unprefixed keys (SEP-414). The server extracts them as the remote parent, and the MCP client span becomes the parent of the server span whatever the transport. The MCP revision 2026-07-28 reserves these three keys in `_meta` as an exception to the vendor-prefix rule and requires W3C formats [[r6]] [[r7]].

explain.title: Context crossing an A2A hop and an MCP hop
explain.alt: An orchestrator sends an A2A request with a traceparent HTTP header to a remote agent. The remote agent calls an MCP server, putting traceparent into params underscore meta. All spans share one trace id.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Orchestrator
  participant R as Remote agent
  participant M as MCP server
  O->>R: A2A request, traceparent header
  R->>M: tools/call, params._meta traceparent
  M-->>R: Result
  R-->>O: Task with artifact

explain.md: **A2A** defines no tracing fields of its own. Its enterprise guidance says clients and servers should participate in distributed tracing, for example by propagating W3C Trace Context headers over HTTP, and should log `taskId`, `sessionId`, correlation ids and trace context [[r9]]. The Agent Framework documentation does not say whether its A2A client and server forward `traceparent`: UNVERIFIED (checked 2026-10-13).

explain.title: Baggage travels to third parties
explain.md: Baggage is propagated across service boundaries and to third-party APIs, so do not put passwords, keys or personal data in it [[r17]]. Strip or restrict baggage at organization boundaries.

whereToUse: A multi-agent system where an orchestrator calls specialist agents over A2A
An agent that calls MCP servers run by other teams and needs end-to-end latency
A background or durable run that continues after the original request returned
Debugging which hop added latency or lost an error
Security reviews of what identifiers leave the organization with each request

use: Propagate W3C trace context on every hop you control, including MCP `_meta`
Use client-opened MCP transports when you need an end-to-end trace
Log `taskId`, `contextId` and trace id together at every A2A boundary
avoid: Do not assume provider-hosted MCP tools or third-party agents continue your trace
Do not forward baggage with sensitive values to external parties
Do not let each service sample independently: a trace must be kept or dropped as a whole
flips: A hop is a provider-hosted tool: accept a gap and correlate by call ids and timestamps
The peer is another organization: propagate trace context only if both sides agree, and keep correlation ids either way
The work continues after a restart: persist context with the task and link the new trace to the old one

pitfalls.symptom: A trace stops at the agent's `execute_tool` span and the MCP server starts a new trace
pitfalls.cause: The tool was a provider-hosted MCP tool, so the framework did not inject `params._meta` context
pitfalls.fix: Use a client-opened MCP transport (for example `MCPStreamableHTTPTool`) when you need end-to-end tracing [[r10]]

pitfalls.symptom: The peer agent's work appears as a separate trace
pitfalls.cause: No `traceparent` header was sent or the peer ignored it, and the A2A spec has no tracing fields
pitfalls.fix: Send the header, verify the peer extracts it and log `taskId` on both sides as a fallback [[r9]]

pitfalls.symptom: Only part of each trace is stored
pitfalls.cause: Downstream services made independent sampling decisions instead of honoring the parent's
pitfalls.fix: Use consistent trace-ID-based head sampling, or tail sampling in a collector, so a trace is kept or dropped as a whole [[r20]]

scenarios.title: An external partner's agent in the middle of a request
scenarios.situation: An orchestrator calls a partner's agent over A2A. The partner runs its own telemetry. Requests contain customer data and legal limits what identifiers cross the boundary.
unknowns: Does a contract cover sharing trace ids?
scenarios.question: How do you keep the request debuggable?

options.name: Send `traceparent` only if agreed, strip baggage, and log `taskId` and `contextId` on both sides
options.why: You get a joinable trail without leaking internal labels or assuming the partner continues your trace.
options.tradeoff: No single waterfall: joins are manual.

options.name: Forward all context including baggage
options.why: Baggage travels to third parties and could expose internal tags or user data.
options.tradeoff: Right inside your own trust boundary.

options.name: Send nothing and rely on timestamps
options.tradeoff: Hard to join incidents and impossible to attribute latency by hop.

flips.if: Both companies run compatible tracing and agree to share ids

flips.then: Ask for a correlation header in the contract.

scenarios.takeaway: Cross-organization context sharing is a decision, not a default.

scenarios.title: An agent using a provider-hosted MCP tool
scenarios.situation: An agent uses an MCP tool hosted by the model provider's runtime. Slow tool calls are the main incident cause and the team wants end-to-end traces.
constraints: Tool server is run by your own team
unknowns: Can the agent open the MCP connection itself?
Does the tool server extract `_meta` context?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Switch to a client-opened MCP transport so the framework injects `params._meta`
options.why: The agent process makes the call, so context is injected and the server span joins the trace.
options.tradeoff: The agent needs network access to the server and you lose provider-side convenience.

options.name: Keep the hosted tool and correlate by call id and timestamps
options.why: No code change and still lets you join logs.

options.name: Assume propagation works and skip verification
options.why: The framework does not inject context for provider-managed MCP calls, so traces break silently.
options.tradeoff: Safe only if the tool server already links by other means.

flips.then: Keep the hosted tool and rely on correlation ids.
Verify behavior directly, since the docs describe it for Python only.

scenarios.takeaway: Check who makes the call, because that process injects the context.

quiz.q: How does trace context travel on an MCP `tools/call` request?
quiz.explain: The conventions inject W3C context into `params._meta`, and MCP revision 2026-07-28 reserves those unprefixed keys. Tool arguments are model-controlled data and should not carry trace context.

quiz.q: A trace breaks at an MCP call. Which causes fit the documented Agent Framework behavior? Select all that apply.
options: The tool is a provider-managed MCP tool, so the provider runtime makes the call
The agent opened the MCP session itself with a streamable HTTP tool
The server does not extract `_meta` trace context
A global propagator was configured to something other than W3C
quiz.explain: Hosted tools skip injection, a server that ignores `_meta` cannot join the trace, and the framework injects through the global propagators, so a mismatched propagator changes the format. A client-opened session is the case that does inject context.

quiz.q: What is the main risk of forwarding W3C `baggage` on every call?
options: It propagates across service boundaries and to third-party APIs, so sensitive values can leak
quiz.explain: Baggage is propagated to downstream and third-party services. It does not affect sampling, tokens or `traceparent`.

flashcards.front: What does a `traceparent` header look like?
flashcards.back: `00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>`. W3C Trace Context Level 1 is a Recommendation (2021-11-23).

flashcards.front: Where does MCP carry trace context?
flashcards.back: In `params._meta` as `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage`. MCP 2026-07-28 reserves these keys.

flashcards.front: When does Agent Framework not inject MCP trace context?
flashcards.back: For provider-hosted or provider-managed MCP tools, because the provider runtime makes the call. Client-opened MCP sessions do get context in Python.
No. Its guidance says to propagate W3C Trace Context over HTTP and to log `taskId`, `sessionId` and correlation ids.
